description: Cooks every Sunday and keeps making dishes. Studies Japanese on their own, chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture, watches anime and wants to visit Kyoto. Has three side projects.
tests: When one topic shows up repeatedly across different contexts (self-study, elective class, anime, travel), the topic-level generalization IS allowed. Guards against being so cautious that nothing is promoted
A clear self-statement ("I cook every Sunday... it's my reset") is promoted after one mention
Dishes are appended as separate records, not merged into one sentence
"Yesterday" in a message dated 9/13 is recorded as 9/12
Three projects mentioned once are grouped as records under one projects category; the robot arm's progress is appended

observations.note: They made shakshuka that morning with cumin and a bit of feta, and described it as easy.
They say they cook every Sunday as a reset for the week, and that chopping vegetables clears their head. They usually choose what to make that morning based on what is in the fridge.
observations.hook: Chopping vegetables as a way to clear their head
observations.quote: I cook every Sunday no matter what. It's my reset for the week, chopping vegetables just clears my head.

observations.note: They made ramen from scratch, using chicken shoyu broth. The broth took seven hours, and they found the tare the hardest part.
observations.quote: Made ramen from scratch yesterday. Took me 7 hours for the broth lol

observations.note: They have been learning Japanese with Duolingo for about three months and say they chose to learn it on their own.
observations.quote: Nobody asked me to learn it, I just wanted to.

observations.note: While making ramen, they read some of the Japanese on a soy sauce label and felt proud of doing so.
observations.hook: Seeing a skill they had been practicing become usable in an everyday setting
observations.caveat: They could read only some of the label.
observations.quote: I could read the label on the soy sauce bottle. Kinda proud of that.

observations.note: They chose a Japanese history elective to understand the culture behind food and a language they are interested in, and asked beyond the syllabus how sakoku affected Edo people's food and whether sushi came from that era.
observations.topic: Cultural history of food and language
observations.hook: Understanding the cultural context behind food and language, including how historical conditions shaped everyday eating.
observations.quote: I picked this elective because I wanted to understand the culture behind the food and the language I'm into.

observations.note: They found the idea of sushi as fast food funny.
observations.hook: The unexpected contrast of a familiar food being described as fast food in its historical setting.
observations.quote: Sushi as fast food is so funny.

observations.note: They said they were sad after finishing Frieren; they did not say which part of the show affected them most.
observations.quote: I just finished Frieren and I'm sad it's over.

observations.note: They said temple scenes in anime always get them, pointing to the appeal of seeing those settings depicted. They want to visit Kyoto someday and are saving for a possible trip next year.
observations.quote: the temple scenes in anime always get me

observations.note: They want to visit Kyoto someday and are saving toward the trip, perhaps for next year.
observations.hook: Visiting Kyoto after being drawn in by temple scenes in anime
observations.caveat: Maybe next year; no firm date stated.
observations.quote: I really want to go to Kyoto someday
